articles.title: Grocery Stores Become Sought-After Destinations for Travelers
articles.summary: A growing trend sees travelers seeking out unique experiences at local grocery stores abroad, with many offering hands-on workshops and high-end products.
articles.content: A group of friends rented a chalet in Courchevel, France for a friend's birthday last winter, and I was tasked with buying groceries. I headed to Sherpa Supermarché, a grocery chain with 116 locations across the French mountains, expecting a quick shopping trip that would be over in no time. But what I found at Sherpa far exceeded my expectations - its cheese section was staggering, boasting an impressive array of Comté varieties that left me bewildered. Travelers are increasingly seeking out grocery stores as part of their international experiences, with 77 percent saying they enjoy visiting them abroad, according to Hilton's 2026 Travel Trends Report. A personal experience in an IGA store in Montréal still stands out - the revelation that Canadian potato chip flavors far surpass those available at home left a lasting impression. Similarly, a trip to Seoul introduced the writer to Lotte Mart's wide variety of instant noodles and elaborate packaged desserts, showcasing the unique aspects of local cuisine. Grocery stores like Big C in Thailand offer more than just shopping, with hands-on workshops where visitors can taste Thai curry pastes - an experience that highlights the cultural nuances found in everyday shopping. Other travelers have raved about a supermarket in Panama City, Super K, which claims to be the world's largest kosher supermarket and is said to sell exceptional babka. Grocery stores are increasingly becoming sought-after destinations for travelers, with high-end options offering an upscale experience. In Los Angeles, Erewhon has gained a reputation as a hub for wellness enthusiasts, where visitors can observe the city's elite paying top dollar for premium products and services. The store's offerings include celebrity-endorsed smoothies at $22 each, catering to those seeking a luxurious shopping experience. This trend of luxury grocery shopping is being emulated in other cities around the world. New York City's Meadow Lane has also joined the ranks of high-end grocery stores, with its beautifully packaged pantry staples and artisanal chicken fingers that are almost too good to care about their $17 price tag. The store's upscale atmosphere and premium products have made it a sought-after destination for shoppers looking for a luxurious experience. Meanwhile, in Tokyo, Kayanoya has opened a new flagship store in Ginza, designed by renowned architect Kengo Kuma. Vacuum-sealed purchases have made it easier than ever to bring home edible souvenirs from Paris, with La Grande Épicerie streamlining the process. The result is a seamless shopping experience that allows visitors to focus on exploring the city rather than worrying about transporting their finds. The cheese case in Courchevel proved to be an unexpected highlight of my trip, yielding more insight into the town's character than its upscale supper clubs. By venturing beyond the usual tourist haunts and monuments, I discovered a different side of the place, one that is just as telling as any guidebook or map. articles.title: Federal Aviation Administration Outage Leads to 18,000+ Flight Cancellations
articles.summary: Millions of passengers were affected by the recent Federal Aviation Administration outage that led to widespread flight cancellations.
articles.content: Air travel disruptions have reached unprecedented levels, with recent events causing significant chaos for millions of passengers. The Federal Aviation Administration's recent outage led to a staggering 18,000+ flight cancellations over just three days, leaving many travelers scrambling to adjust their plans. In the past few years, various factors such as bad weather, government shutdowns, and technical glitches have caused major travel disruptions. TPG reporters, who cover these issues regularly, have occasionally found themselves stranded at airports due to similar circumstances. Airport chaos can be unpredictable, but being prepared is key. One essential tip is to act quickly when trouble arises. When flights are delayed or canceled, passengers need to think on their feet and respond swiftly to minimize the impact. To stay ahead of the game, it's crucial to download your airline's app before your trip and familiarize yourself with its features. In addition, opt-in for all available text messages, push notifications, and alerts to receive timely updates about flight changes or cancellations. When booking a backup flight with miles, it's essential to consider potential consequences on your original reservation. Airlines may cancel one of your reservations if they detect possible duplicate bookings, which can lead to a lost opportunity or wasted points. To avoid this issue, carefully review the airline's policies regarding duplicate bookings and basic economy tickets. Some carriers will return miles if you decide to cancel a backup flight, but it's crucial to understand their refund policies beforehand. If you do opt for a backup ticket on your original airline, be prepared for the possibility of cancellation due to system-detecting duplicate bookings. When dealing with mass flight disruptions, it's crucial to be prepared for the possibility of a long stay at your destination. If you find yourself in a situation where flights are grounded and departures are scarce, it may be wise to cut your losses and book a hotel room as soon as possible. According to Eric Rosen, a member of our team, this is especially important when rooms near airports start to dwindle quickly during such crises. A hotel stay can provide much-needed comfort and convenience, especially if you're stuck overnight due to flight cancellations or delays. In fact, some travelers have reported that empty rooms near airports can vanish rapidly in the face of widespread travel disruptions. Having your confirmation number ready is essential when dealing with airline customer service representatives. Airline lounges often have dedicated customer assistance desks, which can be a more efficient way to resolve issues compared to waiting on the concourse. In fact, some travelers have found that lounge queues are significantly shorter than those on the main airport floor. For instance, Delta's Sky Club in Philadelphia has seen its fair share of customers seeking help with flight disruptions. However, it's worth noting that representatives at credit card-affiliated lounges may not be able to assist with reservation changes or cancellations since they don't work directly for the airline. Before approaching an airline representative, travelers can prepare by researching available flights and presenting their options. Ben Mutzabaugh, managing editor of aviation, suggests looking up alternative routes and presenting them to the agent as potential solutions. This can help expedite the process and increase the chances of finding a suitable flight. For example, if a traveler's original flight is canceled, they might say, I see that another airline has a non-cancelled flight to my destination. When dealing with flight disruptions, it's essential to be persistent in searching for a replacement flight. This involves repeatedly checking airline websites, online travel agencies, and other booking platforms for available options. If the ideal flight isn't immediately available, don't give up, rebooking options may still become available as airlines adjust their schedules. According to TPG's Clint Henderson, it's crucial to keep checking for alternative flights. Flight disruptions can be frustrating, but staying vigilant is key to finding a suitable replacement. Airlines often offer rebooking options when flights are delayed or canceled, so it's worth exploring these possibilities. In some cases, the ideal flight may not be available, but this doesn't mean all hope is lost, other options may arise as airlines adjust their schedules. The airline's website should be regularly checked for updates on the status of your original flight and potential rebooking opportunities. articles.title: Ancient Materials Revisited in Modern Jewelry Design
articles.summary: A surge of creativity is sweeping through the world of jewelry, with designers pushing the boundaries of traditional materials by incorporating unconventional substances such as glass, wood, and porcelain.
articles.content: A surge of creativity is sweeping through the world of jewelry, with designers pushing the boundaries of traditional materials. Unlike clothing, which has strict limitations in terms of fabric and texture, jewelry can be crafted from an astonishing array of substances, so long as they are durable enough to withstand wear. Ancient civilizations were already experimenting with glass in their jewelry, with evidence showing that it was used as far back as 3500 BCE in Mesopotamia and Egypt, where it was fashioned into beads and intricate carvings. Designers today are revisiting this humble material, along with wood, porcelain, and other unconventional substances. This trend makes perfect sense, given the current era of experimental jewelry, which is all about bold shapes and silhouettes that make a statement. Fine jewelers are now incorporating a wide range of materials into their work, from collaboration pieces to entirely new creations. The surge in precious metal prices has led to a significant shift in the jewelry market, causing fashion insiders and collectors to reevaluate their collections. As a result, traditional solid gold pieces are becoming increasingly rare and expensive, prompting buyers to seek out more affordable alternatives that still offer unique aesthetic appeal. This trend is driving designers to experiment with unconventional materials, such as wood, which is prized for its natural warmth and organic feel. Designers like Colin Keane Lynch of Keane New York are now working with glass, creating intricate pieces that can mimic the appearance of other materials through innovative use of form, texture, and color. The allure of unconventional materials in jewelry design continues to grow, with various brands opting for alternatives to traditional precious stones and metals. Thatch, a brand co-founded by Amy Goin and Laura Laing, is one such example. Its offerings include substantial wooden heart pendants alongside fish-shaped wooden bangles and charms. Goin's perspective on wood as a material resonates with her brand's ethos: "We feel that wood holds energy the same way gemstones do," she says. This affinity for wood stems from its distinct, quieter energy - one that is more grounded and soulful compared to traditional gemstones. The raw, unpolished nature of wood adds to its unique character. Thatch's use of wood in jewelry design stands as a testament to the creative possibilities that alternative materials offer. As consumers increasingly seek out distinctive, meaningful pieces, brands like Thatch are meeting this demand with innovative designs that celebrate the natural beauty of unconventional materials. The breakthrough lies in an initiative called Licensed Weights, which enables customers to tailor MAI's frontier models to suit their specific needs and run them securely on Azure. This approach contrasts with the more restrictive proprietary models from OpenAI and Anthropic, yet doesn't grant full access like Hugging Face's offerings do. Companies can get started by working through their Microsoft account representatives. Microsoft AI CEO Mustafa Suleyman emphasized that customers retain control over who accesses their customized models, ensuring data security and ownership remain in their hands. This selective approach to open-weight AI has sparked interest among businesses, which will now need to partner with MAI's Frontier Company for delivery of custom models embedded within their products. These collaborations promise a seamless integration of tailored AI capabilities into various applications, underlining Microsoft's commitment to empowering its customers through cutting-edge technology. Businesses are increasingly seeking AI solutions that allow them to maintain control over their intellectual property. To meet this need, Microsoft has introduced Licensed Weights, a customizable AI model framework that lets companies tailor their own AI capabilities using their proprietary data. According to Suleyman, "no one wants to pour their IQ into someone else's model." This sentiment echoes the views of Palantir CEO Alex Karp, who has repeatedly argued that businesses should be able to utilize their valuable information within their own AI models. By offering Licensed Weights, Microsoft is providing a middle ground between proprietary and open-source AI options. The traditional narrative surrounding AI has pitted expensive, proprietary models with peak capabilities against cheaper, open-source alternatives that offer customizability but often lack performance. However, by introducing a customizable option, Microsoft may be able to bridge this gap and carve out a unique position for itself in the market. Western research labs are now developing more competitive open-weight models, including those from Thinking Machines and Mistral. Nonetheless, Anthropic and OpenAI still hold a significant majority of the enterprise AI market share. With Licensed Weights, Microsoft is diversifying its offerings and differentiating itself from other major players in the industry. Microsoft's new Licensed Weights offering has allowed businesses to customize AI models using their own data, setting it apart from other major players in the industry. The company's MAI Code 2 model, unveiled at Ignite 2026 alongside Copilot Workspaces, boasts impressive performance numbers on widely used benchmarks. According to Suleyman, the model achieves 98% of the performance of GPT 6.1 Sol at just 40% of the cost, and significantly outperforms Opus 5.5 in terms of price and quality. With Licensed Weights, Microsoft is now positioned as a reliable choice for organizations seeking a tailored blend of ROI tools, customization capabilities, security controls, and flexibility - all while keeping costs low. articles.title: Alpha School Faces Disappointing AI Tool Usage
articles.summary: Despite offering an exceptional AI-powered tool, students are not using it as intended at Alpha School.
articles.content: A pioneering education project has hit a significant snag after investing heavily in artificial intelligence to support student learning. Alpha School, a cutting-edge educational platform that's been gaining national attention, is now facing a stark reality: despite offering an exceptional AI-powered tool, students are not using it as intended. The AI study aid was designed to fill the gap between human tutoring sessions, providing personalized math practice and real-time feedback. With over 10,000 exercises and a patient AI assistant on hand, students could have benefited from seamless support at any time. But the numbers tell a different story: only about one in ten students opted for this advanced learning tool. Moreover, many who did start using it soon lost interest and dropped out altogether. The disappointing usage rate raises important questions about how education technology is being implemented in schools, particularly as Alpha School expands into public institutions in Texas and South Carolina, where districts are considering a significant shift towards AI-driven instruction. Students who used Khan Academy's AI tutor in Tennessee middle schools showed limited engagement, with most messages consisting of brief answers or clicks on suggested prompts. Despite nearly every student trying the tool, the median student interacted with it in less than a third of practice days and only 17% of sessions where mistakes were made. These findings mirror Khan Academy's own reports that approximately 15% of students with access to the AI tutor actually use it. However, when human tutors took charge of managing students' learning, a significant shift occurred. In this setup, each student's tutor selected practice exercises tailored to their needs, assigned tasks, and followed up at subsequent lessons. This new approach led to increased completion rates for assignments, with more than half of students fulfilling their commitments compared to about 10% who used the app independently. The change was remarkable because it involved the same app and exercises as before. The only difference was the introduction of a human element, a tutor familiar with each student's progress and expectations. This hybrid model is now being replicated in Tutorela, an education platform built on the understanding that human interaction can significantly boost engagement and learning outcomes. Tutorela's designers were motivated by this discovery to create a system that combines AI support with personalized guidance from educators. By placing humans at the forefront of student learning, they aim to make a more substantial impact than relying solely on technology. The success of this approach underscores the importance of balancing technological innovation with human interaction in education. As platforms like Tutorela expand into new markets and institutions, it remains to be seen whether their hybrid model can replicate these results at scale. The limitations of AI-driven education tools have become apparent in our own experiments. Despite providing high-quality content and instant feedback, student participation remained low. It appears that personalized learning materials alone are insufficient to motivate students. In our experience, the quality of educational content is not the primary issue. Students today have access to a vast array of free, high-quality explanations online. However, this wealth of information does not automatically translate into improved academic performance. The absence of human interaction and accountability seems to be the critical factor in determining student engagement. A child may complete worksheets generated by AI, but without someone to hold them accountable for their work, they are less likely to put in effort. This dynamic was evident in our own research. AI can certainly augment the tutoring process by providing additional support between lessons. It can offer explanations and practice materials that human tutors cannot match. However, this is only effective when a tutor sets the direction and goals for the student's learning. The problem arises when AI assumes a more prominent role, replacing human interaction altogether. In such cases, students may feel less motivated to engage with the material, as there is no one to hold them accountable for their progress. Ultimately, school leaders must consider how they will ensure that students use these tools effectively. Simply relying on the software itself may not be enough, as our research and others have shown. To make AI tools effective for parents, it's crucial to pair them with human support. This approach is a far cry from relying solely on automated learning systems. A teacher or tutor can set clear goals and provide regular check-ins, helping students stay on track and addressing any issues that may arise. By combining the strengths of both humans and AI, education can become more personalized and engaging. The future of learning will not replace human instructors with machines but rather augment their role with technology. To succeed in today's rapidly changing landscape, companies must be agile and adaptable. They need to stay attuned to shifting consumer needs and technological advancements. This means building organizations that can pivot quickly in response to new opportunities and challenges. Effective leaders recognize the importance of adaptability and build their teams accordingly. By fostering a culture of continuous learning and innovation, they empower their organizations to thrive in an ever-evolving world. articles.title: EcoTailor Mobile App Generates Personalized Low-Carbon Daily Schedules
articles.summary: A team of researchers has created a mobile app called EcoTailor, which generates personalized low-carbon daily schedules for users based on their commitments, transportation options, and preferences.
articles.content: A team of researchers has created EcoTailor, a mobile app that generates personalized low-carbon daily schedules for users based on their commitments, transportation options, and preferences. The system was developed by Professor Inseok Hwang's team at Pohang University of Science and Technology, in collaboration with integrated MS-Ph.D. students Jeongwon Choi and Donghyeon Kang. Their work was presented at the ACM UbiComp/ISWC 2026 conference and published in Proceedings of the ACM on Interactive, Mobile, Wearable and Ubiquitous Technologies. While many people acknowledge the need to reduce carbon emissions, they often struggle to make environmentally friendly choices due to various constraints. For instance, taking public transportation might be impractical when time is limited before an appointment, while walking may feel too demanding on a particularly tiring day. In contrast to existing sustainability technologies that focus on raising awareness of carbon emissions or encouraging greener behaviors, EcoTailor takes into account multiple interconnected factors that influence people's daily decisions. These include time constraints, cost considerations, physical effort required, appointments, and even weather conditions. The goal is to create a more practical approach to reducing carbon emissions by making environmentally friendly options align with users' existing schedules and preferences. By doing so, the researchers aim to make sustainable living a more attainable reality for individuals in their daily lives. The researchers behind EcoTailor recognized that daily schedules are not static and can vary greatly from person to person and even from one day to another. Certain commitments, such as classes or appointments, may be inflexible, but other activities like writing reports or exercising can often be rescheduled or relocated. Daily circumstances also play a significant role in determining available choices. For instance, bad weather might make outdoor activities less feasible, while fatigue could impact the ability to engage in strenuous tasks. These fluctuations are crucial factors that EcoTailor takes into account when generating daily schedule options. EcoTailor's mobile system generates multiple low-carbon daily schedule alternatives based on users' individual circumstances. Rather than prescribing a single "best" schedule for minimizing carbon emissions, it offers several options for users to choose from, allowing them to select the one that best suits their day. The innovation behind EcoTailor lies in its ability to reorganize the daily schedule itself. By moving an activity to a slightly different time or location, users can create opportunities for more environmentally friendly choices, such as walking instead of driving. The researchers behind EcoTailor conducted a four-week study to assess its effectiveness in reducing carbon emissions. Participants used the system in their daily lives, evaluating its impact on their environmental footprint. Results showed an average decrease of 5.48% and a maximum reduction of 22.4% in estimated daily carbon emissions associated with transportation and occupying places. These findings suggest that EcoTailor can make a significant difference in reducing our ecological impact. Throughout the study, participants explored various schedule options suggested by EcoTailor, selecting those that best suited their needs and making adjustments as necessary. By incorporating low-carbon plans into their routines, users were able to make sustainable choices more practical. EcoTailor's approach focuses on empowering individuals to make environmentally friendly decisions without sacrificing convenience. Rather than prescribing the most eco-friendly solution, it offers flexible alternatives tailored to each person's schedule and circumstances. The system's creators believe that EcoTailor has the potential to go beyond environmental sustainability, integrating values such as health and well-being into users' daily lives. Personalized planning technologies like EcoTailor could help people naturally adopt a broader range of priorities in their everyday routines. Personalized planning technologies like EcoTailor are designed to help individuals naturally adopt a broader range of priorities in their daily routines by scheduling low-carbon activities. These systems use various inputs such as personal preferences and habits to create customized plans that minimize environmental impact while accommodating individual needs. By incorporating factors like transportation modes, energy usage, and food choices, EcoTailor aims to make sustainable living more accessible and achievable for a wider audience. articles.summary: The National Republican Senatorial Committee is preparing for a tough election cycle with 19 GOP seats to defend and at least six more to flip.
articles.content: Bernie Moreno is about to take on a daunting task as the incoming chair of the National Republican Senatorial Committee. With 19 GOP seats to defend in 2028 and at least six more to flip for a majority, he's painting a grim picture. "It's absolutely a savagely brutal map," the Ohio Republican bluntly stated, highlighting the challenges ahead. Republicans are facing a tough road after being dealt a historic blow in the midterms, with just 44 seats likely heading into the next election cycle. Moreno's party must navigate a delicate balance of holding onto crucial battleground states like Wisconsin and North Carolina while making inroads in Democratic strongholds such as Arizona, Pennsylvania, Georgia, and Nevada. The latter four are held by Sens. Mark Kelly, John Fetterman, Raphael Warnock, and Catherine Cortez Masto. To tackle this daunting task, Moreno's team has been conducting interviews with several candidates for the key role of NRSC executive director over the past few days. Sources close to the matter have revealed that a handful of hopefuls have been vetted by the committee chair-elect and his inner circle. The Senate GOP committee faces a challenging road ahead in 2028, as it navigates a complex landscape shaped by the party's relationship with former President Donald Trump and his influence over the primaries. Chris Grant, a seasoned Republican strategist who has worked for several prominent campaigns, is expected to play a key role as outside consultant to the committee. His experience will be crucial in helping the GOP committee chart its course through the treacherous waters of electoral politics. The party's efforts will be further complicated by the presence of lame duck President Trump, whose significant influence over the GOP and its primaries remains unchanged despite his impending departure from office. Moreover, Vice President JD Vance is likely to throw his hat into the ring in 2028, creating an additional layer of complexity for the committee. Moreno's past reluctance to distance himself from Trump has been evident in his willingness to attribute Republican losses to factors other than the president's policies, such as high gas prices. However, the party's electoral rebuke of Trump's economic agenda is prompting a re-evaluation of its alignment with him and his influence. Senate Republicans are facing a daunting task in rebuilding their electoral strength after the party's significant losses in the midterms. Several battleground states that were once considered safe for the GOP have fallen to Democratic control. This shift has left many within the party questioning their alignment with Trump and his influence. The president's decision to back primary challenges against several incumbent Republicans, including John Cornyn of Texas and Bill Cassidy of Louisiana, has been particularly damaging. The move is estimated to have cost the Senate Republican campaign committee over $200 million as they attempted to salvage Ken Paxton's struggling campaign in Texas. This costly effort ultimately proved unsuccessful. Trump's intervention in primary contests has also had far-reaching consequences, with Sen. Thom Tillis deciding to retire from his North Carolina seat rather than face another challenging election. The party now faces the daunting task of finding candidates who can win general elections in highly competitive states while navigating the complex landscape of GOP primaries where Trump will undoubtedly play a significant role. Senate Republicans are well aware that they cannot afford to field weak or untested candidates in 2028, as seen with the implosions of Paxton and other hand-picked Trump allies. "There will be no patience for bad recruits this cycle," said a senior Republican, speaking on condition of anonymity to discuss internal conversations. The White House has pointed reporters to comments made by Donald Trump after the midterm elections, where he attributed his party's losses to not being on the ballot and claimed credit for bringing several candidates closer to victory. Senate Majority Leader John Thune and his team are set to play a significant role in recruitment efforts next year, with two individuals involved in the discussions speaking candidly about their plans. Ohio is already drawing attention from Senate hopefuls, including those looking to challenge incoming Democratic Senator Sherrod Brown in 2028. Moreno's search for a Republican recruit has begun. In Ohio, former state Senator Kevin Coughlin is reportedly considering a potential bid for the Senate seat that will be up for grabs in 2028. Ohio Republicans are keeping a close eye on Rep. Mike Turner's seat after his recent loss in reelection. They're aware that Turner's departure could create an opportunity for a prominent figure from their party to take the position. Several Ohio Republicans have been mentioned as potential candidates, but one name keeps popping up: JD Vance. "JD Vance would be a dream candidate," said an Ohio Republican insider. articles.title: Nubia Redmagic 12 Pro Features Cutting-Edge Specs and Large Display
articles.summary: The Nubia Redmagic 12 Pro offers top-notch performance, long battery life, and a large display, making it a go-to choice for mobile gamers.
articles.content: Nubia's Redmagic series has long been a go-to choice for mobile gamers seeking top-notch performance and long battery life. The latest addition to this lineup, the Redmagic 12 Pro, promises to deliver on these fronts with its cutting-edge specs and large display. One of the standout features of the Redmagic 12 Pro is its ability to maintain a cool temperature even during prolonged gaming sessions. This is no small feat, especially considering the phone's powerful processor and high-resolution display. Nubia has clearly put thought into designing a cooling system that can keep up with demanding games. The phone's design, on the other hand, may not be to everyone's taste. The Redmagic 12 Pro sports a boxy shape that is both large and slippery, making it difficult to handle one-handed. This is especially true when trying to scroll through menus or browse the web on its big screen. Nubia has always been willing to take risks with design, and the Redmagic series is no exception. The 12 Pro's translucent industrial aesthetic and RGB lighting are certainly eye-catching, but may not be what everyone wants in their everyday phone. The company's focus on style over substance results in a device that looks impressive but feels awkward to hold. The price of the Redmagic 12 Pro is also a point of contention. Starting at $949, it's clear that Nubia is targeting the high-end market with this release. However, some potential buyers may feel that the compromises made in other areas - such as camera quality and software updates - are not worth the premium price. While the Redmagic 12 Pro has its share of flaws, it remains a compelling option for those seeking a dedicated gaming smartphone. With touch-sensitive shoulder buttons, RGB lighting, and gaming-focused software features, this phone is designed with gamers in mind. The Nubia Redmagic 12 Pro's design is a masterclass in ergonomic gaming handsets, excelling when held in landscape orientation. The substantial frame provides a comfortable grip, making it easy to hold for extended periods of gaming. However, the phone's sleek look comes at the cost of practicality - there's no headphone port, forcing gamers to rely on wireless audio solutions or the built-in speakers. On the other hand, the absence of a camera bump is a refreshing design choice, but it does contribute to the phone's slippery texture. The addition of touch-sensitive shoulder buttons and a dedicated Magic Key for gaming mode adds to the phone's gaming credentials, although users can customize the latter to launch the camera instead. This key has undergone a design change, transitioning from a switch to a red button, yet still retains its position alongside the circular power button. Finger smudges are an inevitable consequence of handling this glass sandwich, and Nubia's toned-down lighting doesn't entirely alleviate the issue. Nevertheless, users can still personalize the lighting settings for various activities, adding a touch of customization to the phone's overall aesthetic. A powerful cooling fan is embedded within the device, with dual vents designed to expel hot air efficiently. Notably, this setup hasn't compromised the phone's water and dust resistance, which boasts an IP68/69 rating. The 6.85-inch OLED display is a true showstopper, boasting an uninterrupted viewing experience courtesy of its lack of notch or cutout camera. An embedded fingerprint sensor at the bottom provides convenient biometric security, while the selfie camera situated under the screen leaves something to be desired in terms of effectiveness. The Nubia Redmagic 12 Pro boasts an impressive combination of hardware components that make it a powerhouse for gaming. At its core lies Qualcomm's Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 chipset, paired with Redmagic's own RedCore R5 chipset and either 12 or 16 GB of RAM. This potent pairing enables the phone to deliver speeds that leave other Android devices in its wake. Benchmark scores are certainly a testament to this phone's capabilities, with the Nubia Redmagic 12 Pro topping the charts above even high-end devices like Samsung's Galaxy S26 Ultra. Gaming performance is equally impressive, allowing users to play demanding titles such as Asphalt Legends and Wuthering Waves at maximum settings without any issues. The phone's cooling system plays a crucial role in maintaining its performance under intense gaming conditions. The dual-loop liquid cooling system, complemented by the fan and vapor chamber, helps keep the device running smoothly even after prolonged periods of use. While some minor thermal throttling may occur, the 12 Pro still manages to deliver an exceptional gaming experience. One notable feature that sets the Nubia Redmagic 12 Pro apart is its dedicated game space called Gravity X. Accessible via a red button, this mode allows users to customize settings and map pressure-sensitive shoulder buttons for optimal gaming performance. The interface also includes an anime companion named Mora, as well as AI-powered assistance. In addition to the various gaming features, the phone's Steam emulator is another exciting aspect of the Nubia Redmagic 12 Pro. Users can log into their Steam account and potentially play a wide range of games on the device, although compatibility may vary depending on the title. Connectivity options are also plentiful, with support for gamepads, mice, keyboards, and even second screens. The Nubia Redmagic 12 Pro's battery life is one of its standout features, boasting an enormous 8,400-mAh capacity that easily lasts through a full day of gaming and still has something left in reserve. With careful use, it's not hard to imagine pushing this phone to two days on a single charge, making it a great option for those who need a device that can keep up with their active lifestyle. However, there is one caveat: the phone doesn't come with a charger in the box, and users will need to purchase a Redmagic charger if they want to take advantage of its fast charging capabilities, which support up to 80-watt wired or wireless charging. The charging process itself takes around an hour and 17 minutes from dead to full, but it's worth noting that you can get about 50 percent charge in just half an hour, making it a decent option for those who need a quick top-up. Despite its impressive battery life, the Nubia Redmagic 12 Pro does have some notable compromises when it comes to its camera system. While the main 50-megapixel camera performs well in most conditions, and there's also a 50-megapixel ultrawide option available, the lack of a telephoto lens means that zoom is limited to 2X cropping. The result is a camera system that, while adequate for casual snapping, struggles with more demanding tasks such as portrait mode or high-zoom photography. This is particularly evident in low-light conditions, where the smaller sensor of the ultrawide camera really starts to show its limitations. The front-facing camera, hidden under the screen, is fine for video calls and well-lit selfies, but shots often look a bit muddy and lack the crispness that users might expect from a device at this price point. The Redmagic OS 12 operating system is a mixed bag, sitting atop Android 17 but feeling like a pale imitation of other systems, particularly when it comes to the aesthetic flourishes borrowed from Apple's Liquid Glass. Some users may find the interface tolerable, although others will be put off by the numerous poor translations and awkward phrasing that mar the overall experience. The inclusion of bloatware is another major drawback, serving little purpose beyond taking up valuable space on the device. Furthermore, Nubia's update commitment is woefully inadequate, promising only two years of platform updates and three years of security software support in the US market, a paltry offering compared to other manufacturers. In contrast, UK-based buyers can expect five years of security updates. For those seeking a more well-rounded Android experience, there are numerous alternatives available that offer superior performance and features without the 12 Pro's significant drawbacks. The Pixel 11 Pro XL, for example, can be purchased on sale at a similar price point, making it an attractive option for buyers looking for a device that balances gaming capabilities with everyday usability. One area where the 12 Pro truly excels is in its performance-and-screen combination, which makes it the top choice for gamers. This is largely due to the powerful chipset, which will likely be featured in other devices soon, although these may come at a higher price point and offer additional features like improved cameras and longer software support. Ultimately, the value of the 12 Pro depends on individual priorities, with some buyers willing to overlook its flaws in favor of its gaming capabilities. However, for those seeking a more comprehensive smartphone experience, there are better options available, albeit perhaps at a slightly higher price point. Wired : https://www.wired.com/review/nubia-redmagic-12-pro/

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto Online Causes Chaos for Unlikely Gamer
articles.summary: A mom who's not much into gaming recently picked up Grand Theft Auto Online on her PS5 and quickly found herself in a chaotic situation while playing with her children.
articles.content: A mom who's not much into gaming recently picked up Grand Theft Auto Online on her PS5 and quickly found herself in a chaotic situation. While playing, she accidentally swung a massive punch that hit one of her children right in the head, causing blood to splatter everywhere and prompting her kids to burst out laughing. Her children were enjoying the violent scene unfolding before their eyes, but their mom was less than amused, having only been playing for a couple of hours at this point. It's clear that Grand Theft Auto Online is still capable of catching players off guard with its intense gameplay, even for those who aren't typically into gaming. Growing up, I spent countless hours playing Grand Theft Auto 3 with my brother, and it remains one of my fondest childhood memories. We'd take turns passing the controller back and forth, cackling with glee every time we got "wasted in the game, and our cousin's house became a haven for video game enthusiasts. Looking back, I remember wondering if video games could ever become more realistic than Grand Theft Auto 3. Fast forward to today, and the release of Grand Theft Auto VI on Thursday is poised to revolutionize the gaming world with its cutting-edge graphics and immersive gameplay. The sheer scale of anticipation surrounding Grand Theft Auto VI is undeniable, with millions of players planning to take time off work or school to experience its cutting-edge graphics and immersive gameplay firsthand. For many fans, GTA has been more than just a popular video game franchise - it's a cultural phenomenon that has played a significant role in their lives. The series' long history of pushing boundaries and sparking controversy has made it a staple of gaming culture. The games have often been seen as a reflection of the desires and anxieties of its target demographic, particularly young men who are drawn to the thrill of virtual mayhem and the freedom to express themselves through the game's narrative. The series' blend of action, adventure, and social commentary has made it a staple of gaming culture. The bond between siblings can be especially strong when they share a common interest in gaming, as seen in the experiences of many fans who have formed lasting connections with their brothers or sisters over GTA games. Conversations often flow more naturally when engaging in activities together, like going for a walk or chatting on a drive. The pandemic's Zoom parties, however, lacked that spontaneity, with participants speaking one at a time and lacking eye contact. Grand Theft Auto Online proved to be an ideal environment for recreating those casual interactions. Players can engage in various activities, making it feel like a virtual world where they have the freedom to do as they please. The game's sandbox nature makes it perfect for exploring different scenarios without worrying about real-world consequences. Players often experience frustration when repeatedly targeted by aggressive opponents, such as the adolescent fighter jet pilot dressed in prison attire. However, my brother and I tended to take a more laid-back approach, choosing not to retaliate. Instead, we would simply hang out, drive around, or watch the sunset together. In-game nightclubs provided an opportunity for us to relax and enjoy music, with real-life musicians performing hour-long sets specifically created for the game. We also spent time browsing in-store outfits, curating looks that felt stylish and put-together, essentially playing a digital version of dressing up dolls. As we continued to explore the virtual world of GTA Online, our interactions began to transcend mere gameplay. We started to form connections with other players from around the globe, creating a sense of camaraderie that felt surprisingly authentic. Our Australian counterparts shared our laid-back approach to gaming, and we spent hours chatting casually about everything from in-game exploits to our personal lives. It was as if we had stumbled upon an online community where friendships could flourish without the constraints of physical proximity. The experience even inspired my parents to join us, much to their own surprise. My mom, who had once been a fierce critic of video games, now found herself immersed in the world of GTA Online, laughing and joking with her children as they navigated its virtual streets. As we spent more time together online, our interactions began to bleed into real life. We started seeking out concerts and exhibitions featuring artists from the game's soundtrack, and even tried to replicate some of the stylish outfits we had created in-game. The influence of Grand Theft Auto (GTA) extends far beyond its virtual world, bleeding into our reality in unexpected ways. Marketing campaigns have taken note of this phenomenon, and Rockstar has cleverly incorporated real-world connections into their promotions. For instance, the company has collaborated with popular TV shows like South Park to showcase exclusive game clips, while The Weather Channel even previewed GTA VI's advanced weather systems. Meanwhile, the game's soundtrack has become a significant marketing tool in its own right, featuring artists such as Sza and Justice whose songs are now being discovered by thousands of new listeners. As video game industry analyst Joost van Dreunen notes, When this moment reaches enough critical mass, I think we will see this whole new model for entertainment more broadly. GTA VI's immense popularity has been building anticipation for years, with many expecting it to become the single greatest-selling entertainment product of all time. Even 13 years after GTA V was released, its role-play servers remain populated and active, a testament to the game's enduring appeal. In response, Rockstar has invested heavily in supporting the game's creator-driven community and has developed detailed content-capture features for the new title. Van Dreunen describes GTA VI as an operating system for people to build upon, a hub that enables unprecedented creative expression. The latest installment in the Grand Theft Auto series is set to build upon its predecessor's legacy, catering to a more diverse audience. GTA VI promises to tackle contemporary issues through satire, much like previous games in the franchise. Critics are already labeling it as woke," but this shift towards inclusivity may be exactly what the series needs to stay relevant. The game's creators seem to be aware of their position in the present moment, using GTA VI as a platform to reflect on societal norms. The player base is expected to undergo significant changes with the introduction of Lucia, a Latina character who will take center stage alongside her male counterpart. This move towards greater representation may prompt fans to examine themselves and their expectations from the series. For some players, this shift in focus could be a welcome change, allowing them to engage with the game on a deeper level. GTA VI is poised to become an experience that not only entertains but also challenges its audience. Wired : https://www.wired.com/story/i-will-never-stop-playing-grand-theft-auto/

articles.title: Groundbreaking Discovery Uncovered in Northern Mongolia Tomb
articles.summary: Archaeologists have unearthed a massive 2,000-year-old tomb belonging to an elite nomad from the Xiongnu Empire in Central Asia.
articles.content: Archaeologists have made a groundbreaking discovery in northern Mongolia, unearthing a massive 2,000-year-old tomb belonging to an elite nomad from the Xiongnu Empire in Central Asia. The tomb is the largest of its kind ever found in Mongolia and contains an impressive array of grave goods, with over 400 artifacts unearthed so far. According to researchers, the excavation at Duurlig Nars took four years to complete, involving a team from the National Museum of Korea working closely with local institutions. Duurlig Nars itself is a significant archaeological site, boasting nearly 300 ancient burial mounds known as kurgans, making it the largest noble burial complex of the Xiongnu Empire. The newly discovered tomb in Mongolia has shed light on the nomadic lifestyle and connections of the Xiongnu Empire, which flourished over 2,000 years ago. Archaeologists have found evidence that these skilled warriors were not only adept at horseback riding but also had extensive trade networks across Eurasia. Measuring approximately 240 feet long and 73 meters in length, the tomb's dimensions are comparable to those of the Great Sphinx of Giza. The rectangular structure features a central passageway extending from it, creating an inverted pyramid-like shape that is roughly 5 meters deep. This unusual design suggests a blend of architectural styles. The discovery of various artifacts within the tomb has provided valuable insights into the occupant's high social status and connections with other cultures. A wooden burial chamber containing a coffin was found in the central chamber, alongside silver-and-quartz horse decorations and a wheel from a lacquered horse-drawn carriage, indicating a luxurious lifestyle. In the Xiongnu tomb, archaeologists discovered 15 flat, overlapping pieces of jade on the bottom of the wooden coffin. These jade fragments were unlike the typical circular "bi" used in Han dynasty burials, instead featuring irregular shapes and intricate designs. Their findings suggest that the Xiongnu may have adopted some burial practices from the Han dynasty but put their own unique twist on them. This interpretation is based on the presence of irregularly shaped jade pieces with elaborate engravings. The presence of a Roman glass cup in the 2,000-year-old Mongolian tomb suggests that its owner may have had international connections. The archaeologists are uncertain about the origins of the transparent glass cup, which features a handle and a distinctive shape. Further analysis is needed to determine where the glass cup was manufactured, but DNA tests on the teeth and hair found in the coffin will help identify the individual buried there. These results will also reveal whether the person had any familial connections with others interred at the Duurlig Nars burial complex. Ultimately, this ancient tomb will provide a more nuanced understanding of Xiongnu society from two millennia ago.
